CDI GPU pod base — the container contract for GPU workloads, and the pod sibling
of opencharly/vm-nvidia.

A GPU container gets its driver from the HOST, not from the image: the kernel
module is host-global, so the driver user-space is injected per container by the
runtime from the NVIDIA container toolkit's CDI spec. This box therefore composes
layer-cdi, which owns that contract and whose plan steps FAIL the build if any
host-coupled driver library or nvidia binary is baked in — the boundary is
enforced, not merely documented.

It deliberately contains NO nvidia-utils, NO LD_LIBRARY_PATH export and NO
nvidia-ctk: those belong to opencharly/vm-nvidia, where the guest owns its own
kernel module and must bake the driver. Mixing the two contracts is what made
every GPU pod demand a host tool in its image; measured 2026-11-18, a pod on this
contract serves CUDA with no /usr/bin/nvidia-ctk present.

## Composition

This box composes:

- `@github.com/opencharly/layer-agent-forwarding:v2026.314.0704`
- `@github.com/opencharly/layer-cdi:v2026.329.2058`
